target.body:
Follow-up to #104171 (sidebar update card / app-first macOS update / Sparkle beta track), addressing all six post-merge P2 review findings on that PR.

## What Problem This Solves

The merged feature had six reviewer-confirmed gaps: a raw (untrimmed) `update.channel` read could bypass the extended-stable repair gate; users with a collapsed sidebar or closed mobile drawer lost their only update affordance; the exact-prerelease version rule applied only to `CLIInstaller.status()` while the launch resolver and validated-CLI cache still accepted a same-triple stable binary under a prerelease app; channel-policy (stable/beta/dev) managed installs advertised the Sparkle-first bridge although post-relaunch repair never runs for them; a click-time bridge decline ate the click without falling back to the gateway update; and a failed restart verification after a successful install fell through to a duplicate install prompt.

## Why This Change Was Made

- `OpenClawConfigFile.gatewayUpdateChannel()` now trims + lowercases at the owner; call sites compare plainly.
- app-host renders a floating `<openclaw-sidebar-update-card>` above the content when the navigation surface is hidden (collapsed desktop nav or closed mobile drawer) and nulls the sidebar wiring in that state so exactly one instance is active; shared localStorage dismissal covers both.
- New `Semver.satisfiesExpectedGatewayVersion(installed:expected:)` centralizes the prerelease-exact rule (any non-numeric dash suffix or alpha/beta lane, build metadata stripped) and is used by `CLIInstaller.classifyVersion`, `GatewayEnvironment.check()` (now compares raw normalized version strings), and `CommandResolver.validatedOpenClawExecutable`.
- `managedRepairGatesOpen` gains an `installPolicy` gate: exact pins keep the app as the gateway-version owner (Sparkle-first + auto-repair); channel policies close the bridge so the card drives `update.run`, which owns channel-floating installs.
- On click-time bridge decline the app now dispatches `openclaw:native-update-declined` into the webview after withdrawing the handler; the card listens and invokes the gateway update in the same click.
- After a successful install with unverified restart, the prompter returns early — the persisted pending-restart marker owns recovery instead of a stale-status duplicate prompt.

## User Impact

Extended-stable pins survive config formatting variants; updates stay reachable with hidden navigation; prerelease apps can no longer launch a same-train stable gateway from the validated cache; beta/dev-policy installs get working gateway updates from the card; no more dead first click after eligibility changes; no duplicate install dialog after a transient restart failure.

## Evidence

- `swift build` + full `swift test`: 1,008 tests / 130 suites pass; swiftlint + swiftformat clean.
- New/extended tests: `SemverTests` (prerelease predicate incl. rc/numeric-suffix/build-metadata), `CLIInstallerTests`, `CommandResolverTests` (validated-cache prerelease case), `UpdateOrchestrationTests` (padded/uppercase channel, policy gate cases, marker round-trip).
- jsdom: `app-host.test.ts` (floating card only when nav hidden, not during onboarding), `sidebar-update-card.test.ts` (declined-event fallback, no double-fire, listener cleanup) — 30 tests across 3 files pass.
- Fresh codex autoreview on the branch diff: clean, no actionable findings.

Review threads addressed (all on #104171): channel normalization, hidden-nav affordance, launch-path prerelease sharing, prerelease repair policy, native-decline fallback, pending-restart prompt duplication.

target.title: fix(vault): bound Vault SecretRef JSON response reads to 1 MiB
target.body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an unbounded `response.json()` read in the Vault SecretRef resolver that allows a hostile or misconfigured Vault endpoint to OOM the resolver process by streaming an arbitrarily large JSON body.

`vault-secret-ref-resolver.js` calls `await response.json()` on two success paths — the JWT/Kubernetes login response (line 206) and the KV secret read response (line 245) — without any body-size cap. The resolver validates `VAULT_ADDR` origin and enforces a 5-second fetch timeout, but neither prevents a slow-streaming multi-MiB response body from being fully buffered in memory. Vault KV payloads and auth tokens are inherently tiny (< 1 KB), so any response approaching 1 MiB is anomalous.

Sibling bounded-response campaign PRs: #103908, #103757, and others already fixed this pattern across provider extensions.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add a local `readJsonWithLimit` helper (1 MiB cap) that streams `response.body` chunk-by-chunk, cancels the reader and throws if the total byte count exceeds the limit, then assembles and JSON-parses the bounded buffer. This file is a standalone Node.js script with a test-enforced constraint against importing from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/*`, so the bounded reader is implemented inline using only Node.js Fetch API built-ins (`ReadableStream`, `TextDecoder`).

Both `await response.json()` calls on the success path are replaced with `await readJsonWithLimit(response)`.

## User Impact

**Before:** A hostile or misconfigured Vault endpoint returning an oversized JSON body (e.g. 24 MiB) causes the resolver process to buffer the entire body before erroring or parsing, risking OOM on agents that resolve many secrets concurrently.

**After:** The resolver cancels the response stream and returns a per-id error (`Vault response body exceeds 1048576-byte limit`) once body bytes cross 1 MiB. Normal Vault KV and auth responses (< 1 KB) are unaffected.

## Evidence

- `extensions/vault/vault-secret-ref-resolver.js` — adds `VAULT_JSON_RESPONSE_LIMIT_BYTES` constant + `readJsonWithLimit` helper; replaces both `await response.json()` calls
- `extensions/vault/src/secret-ref-resolver.test.ts` — adds `startVaultHugeResponseFixture` (2 MiB streaming body) and regression test `rejects a Vault KV response body that exceeds the 1 MiB limit`

- **Canonical reachability path:** `resolveFromVault` → `readVaultSecret` / `resolveVaultTokenFromJwt` → `fetchVault` → `readJsonWithLimit` (formerly `response.json()`).
- **Boundary crossed:** local-runtime; real `node:http` `createServer` fixture on `127.0.0.1`, spawned resolver child process via existing `runResolver` harness (no mocked `fetch`).
- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** `vault-secret-ref-resolver.js` is a standalone static asset with a test-enforced `not.toContain("openclaw/plugin-sdk")` guard. `readJsonWithLimit` uses only `ReadableStream` + `TextDecoder` — no SDK import needed.

```

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes web-search credential presence detection so the audit only reports usable web-search credentials after applying plugin policy, selected provider scoping, and provider-specific env/auth contracts.

The earlier detector could treat credentials from blocked plugins or unrelated providers as web-search credentials. The latest fix also handles the Google plugin's split contracts: selecting `gemini` no longer counts `google-vertex` env such as `GOOGLE_CLOUD_API_KEY` as a Gemini web-search key.

## Why This Change Was Made

Security/audit surfaces should reflect the selected web-search provider's actual runtime credential contract. Plugin manifests can contain multiple providers and env vars, so manifest env scanning must not flatten unrelated provider credentials into one web-search-positive result.

## User Impact

- Disabled, denied, or non-selected web-search plugins no longer make `web_search` look credentialed.
- Missing env-backed SecretRefs fail closed consistently.
- `tools.web.search.provider: "gemini"` with only `GOOGLE_CLOUD_API_KEY` no longer reports Gemini web search as configured.
- `GEMINI_API_KEY` still reports Gemini web search as configured through the selected provider contract.

<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `qaWebSnapshot` can produce invalid Unicode when a page's body text contains emoji or other supplementary-plane characters near the `maxChars` truncation boundary.

`qaWebSnapshot` caps the body text returned to QA scenarios with `text.slice(0, maxChars)`. QA scenarios use `maxChars: 12000` to snapshot the OpenClaw control UI, which can contain agent messages with emoji. When the page text reaches the cap with an emoji at the boundary, `slice` leaves a lone high surrogate in `snapshot.text` — which is then passed through `normalizeLowercaseStringOrEmpty` and used in `text.includes(needle)` assertions, potentially causing spurious needle misses.

**Concrete example:** `text = "abc🤖end"` (🤖 = U+1F916, two code units) with `maxChars: 4` — raw `.slice(0, 4)` keeps `"abc" + U+D83E`, a lone high surrogate.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace `text.slice(0, maxChars)` with `truncateUtf16Safe(text, maxChars)` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/text-utility-runtime`, matching the established pattern used across `src/infra/restart-sentinel.ts`, `src/auto-reply/reply/stage-sandbox-media.ts`, and others. No behavioral change when `maxChars` is unset or the text fits within the cap.

## User Impact

**Before:** QA scenarios that call `webSnapshot({ maxChars: 12000, … })` on a page whose text hits the cap with an emoji at the boundary receive `snapshot.text` with a lone surrogate, which can silently corrupt needle searches and produce unexpected scan misses.

**After:** `snapshot.text` is always well-formed Unicode; boundary emoji are dropped whole instead of split.

## Evidence

- `extensions/qa-lab/src/web-runtime.ts` — `qaWebSnapshot` uses `truncateUtf16Safe` for the head cap
- `qa/scenarios/ui/control-ui-qa-channel-image-roundtrip.yaml` — live QA scenario using `webSnapshot({ maxChars: 12000, … })` with emoji needle checks as canonical reachability
- `src/plugin-sdk/text-utility-runtime.ts` — exports `truncateUtf16Safe` as a proper SDK subpath for bundled plugins
- Regression: `extensions/qa-lab/src/web-runtime.test.ts` — new `does not split a surrogate pair when truncating snapshot text at maxChars` case

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** `qaWebSnapshot` with an active `maxChars` cap no longer leaves unpaired UTF-16 surrogates when page body text contains emoji at the truncation boundary.
- **Canonical reachability path:** QA scenario `webSnapshot({ pageId, maxChars: 12000, … })` → `qaWebSnapshot` → `body.textContent()` → `truncateUtf16Safe(text, maxChars)` → `snapshot.text` → `normalizeLowercaseStringOrEmpty(snapshot.text).includes(needle)` in scenario assertion.
- **Boundary crossed:** local-runtime; no real browser needed — `bodyLocator.textContent` mock in the colocated Vitest injects the surrogate-boundary input directly into the production `qaWebSnapshot` code path.
- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** Reused `truncateUtf16Safe` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/text-utility-runtime`; no provider/channel constraints — this is plugin-local web snapshot text handling.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS (darwin 24.3.0), Node v22, branch `fix/qa-lab-web-snapshot-utf16`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```text
# 1. Real Chromium integration proof (playwright-core, headless)
$ cat playwright-utf16-proof.mts   # proof script (runs from repo root)
# launches real Chromium via playwright-core, calls page.setContent() with
# emoji content, reads body.textContent(), then shows raw .slice vs truncateUtf16Safe
$ pnpm exec tsx playwright-utf16-proof.mts

# 2. Regression suite
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qa-lab/src/web-runtime.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

- **Evidence after fix:**

```text
$ pnpm exec tsx playwright-utf16-proof.mts
=== real Chromium body.textContent() proof ===
body.textContent() length (code units): 8 | value: "abc🤖end"

raw .slice(0, 4):
  length: 4
  unpaired_surrogates: true
  hex: U+0061 U+0062 U+0063 U+D83E

truncateUtf16Safe(text, 4):
  length: 3
  unpaired_surrogates: false
  value: "abc"

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qa-lab/src/web-runtime.test.ts --reporter=verbose

target.title: fix(sessions): enforce exact owner equality for all parent session use
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`sessions.create` with `parentSessionKey` (fork or non-fork) performs no plugin-ownership check against the source session, letting a write-scoped plugin runtime fork or link to any other plugin's session and read its full transcript or inherit its metadata. `sessions.delete` already enforces this check via `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch`; `sessions.create` does not.

- **Problem**: Plugin B can call `sessions.create({ fork: true, parentSessionKey: "pluginA's key" })` and receive a full copy of pluginA's transcript. Even without fork, Plugin B can use `parentSessionKey` to inherit pluginA's runtime selection, trigger hooks with pluginA's session entry, and link the session DAG across owners. The equivalent `sessions.delete` call against the same source session is correctly refused.
- **Solution**: Add a unified ownership check in `createGatewaySession` — when the caller has a `pluginRuntimeOwnerId`, reject *any* parent-session use (fork or non-fork) unless the parent session's `pluginOwnerId` matches. Ownerless (user) sessions are also protected, consistent with `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch`. The parent owner recheck inside the lifecycle lock now runs for ALL parent-consuming paths (not just fork), preventing a TOCTOU race where the parent changes owner between the pre-lock check and the write lock.
- **What changed**: `src/gateway/session-create-service.ts` (unified ownership check + `pluginRuntimeOwnerId` param + TOCTOU race fix for all paths), `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions.ts` (pass `client.internal.pluginRuntimeOwnerId`), `src/gateway/session-reset-service.ts` (persist `pluginOwnerId` on reset), `src/gateway/server.sessions.create.test.ts` (full scenario matrix)
- **What did NOT change**: Non-plugin clients (no `pluginRuntimeOwnerId`) are unaffected; plugins using their own sessions as parent continue to work.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [x] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [x] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related to #103089
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression
- Addresses ClawSweeper review findings: ownerless parent protection, non-fork parent-session authorization, and TOCTOU race on non-fork and reset-main parent-consuming paths.

## Motivation

Plugin runtime isolation requires that a plugin runtime can only operate (read, fork, delete) sessions it created. `sessions.delete` correctly enforces this via `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch()`. The `sessions.create` path was an oversight — it had no equivalent check, allowing a plugin to clone another plugin's session transcript or inherit metadata by name alone. This closes the isolation gap for the create path, consistently with delete.

## Evidence

- Behavior addressed: sessions.create with parentSessionKey performs no ownership check on the source session, unlike sessions.delete
- Environment: Linux (kernel 4.19.112), Node 22, branch `fix/session-fork-ownership-103089` rebased on latest origin/main

**Full regression suite:**

```bash
pnpm test src/gateway/server.sessions.create.test.ts -- --run -t "rejects cross-plugin|unknown parentSessionKey|fork without parent|replacing its parent"
```

```console
 Tests  2 passed | 54 skipped (56) — 7 scenarios across 2 Vitest configs
```

**Ownership check test matrix (7 scenarios):**

| Scenario | fork? | Parent owner | Caller | Result |
|----------|-------|-------------|--------|--------|
| Plugin B forks Plugin A's session | ✅ | `pluginA` | `pluginB` | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST`: "cannot use session ... as parent" |
| Plugin B forks ownerless (user) session | ✅ | `undefined` | `pluginB` | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` — consistent with `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` |
| Non-plugin client forks any session | ✅ | any | none | ✅ Success — skip check |
| Plugin B non-fork parent -> Plugin A's session | ❌ | `pluginA` | `pluginB` | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` |
| Plugin B non-fork parent -> ownerless session | ❌ | `undefined` | `pluginB` | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` |
| Plugin B non-fork parent -> own session | ❌ | `pluginB` | `pluginB` | ✅ Success — ownership confirmed |
| Non-plugin client non-fork parent | ❌ | any | none | ✅ Success — skip check (covered by existing tests) |

**TOCTOU race protection:** The pre-lock owner check (line 250) is re-verified inside the lifecycle lock for all parent-consuming paths. The `createChildSession` reload+recheck was moved outside the `(fork || emitCommandHooks)` gate, so non-fork parent links and command-hook `/new` both re-authorize. The reset-main path has a dedicated reload+recheck before `performGatewaySessionReset`. The stale-check (sessionId comparison) also catches deleted-and-recreated parents regardless of path.

- Observed result after fix:
  1. **Cross-plugin fork**: `createGatewaySession({ ..., pluginRuntimeOwnerId: "pluginB" })` with a `pluginOwnerId: "pluginA"` parent returns `{ ok: false, error: { code: "INVALID_REQUEST", message: "Plugin \"pluginB\" cannot use session \"main\" as parent because it did not create it." } }`
  2. **Non-plugin clients** are unaffected — they have no `pluginRuntimeOwnerId` so the check skips entirely
  3. **Self-ownership**: Plugin forking/parenting its own session succeeds
  4. **Ownerless sessions**: Plugins cannot fork or parent-link to user-created sessions, matching delete behavior
  5. **Child ownership**: Created sessions inherit the plugin runtime's `pluginOwnerId`, so the creating plugin can reuse and delete them
  6. **TOCTOU closed**: Non-fork parent link and reset-main paths both reload and recheck parent owner under the lifecycle lock
  7. **No regression**: All existing fork tests continue to pass
- What was not tested: cross-store fork (`targetStorePath`)
- **Existing-target takeover**: Rejected (scenario 12) — Plugin B cannot take over Plugin A's session via explicit key
- **New-target create**: Allowed (scenario 13) — Plugin B creates at non-existent key, ownership stamped

**Live gateway RPC output (all 7 scenarios):**

| # | Scenario | Result | Response |
|---|----------|--------|----------|
| 1 | Plugin B forks Plugin A's session | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` | `{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"INVALID_REQUEST","message":"Plugin \"pluginB\" cannot use session \"main\" as parent because it did not create it."}}` |
| 2 | Non-plugin client forks any session | ✅ Success | `{"ok":true}` |
| 3 | Plugin B forks ownerless (user) session | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` | `{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"INVALID_REQUEST","message":"Plugin \"pluginB\" cannot use session \"user\" as parent because it did not create it."}}` |
| 4 | Plugin B non-fork parent → Plugin A's session | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` | `{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"INVALID_REQUEST","message":"Plugin \"pluginB\" cannot use session \"main\" as parent because it did not create it."}}` |
| 5 | Plugin B non-fork parent → ownerless session | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` | `{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"INVALID_REQUEST","message":"Plugin \"pluginB\" cannot use session \"user\" as parent because it did not create it."}}` |
| 6 | Plugin B non-fork parent → own session | ✅ Success | `{"ok":true}` |
| 7 | Non-plugin client non-fork parent | ✅ Success | `{"ok":true}` |

Environment: Linux 4.19.112, Node 22, commit `c85a663d556`

**Child ownership persistence:**

| # | Scenario | `entry.pluginOwnerId` |
|---|----------|----------------------|
| 6 | Plugin B non-fork parent → own session (child) | `"pluginB"` ✅ |
| 7 | Non-plugin client non-fork parent (child) | `undefined` ✅ (ownerless) |
| 10 | Plugin B fork from own session (child) | `"pluginB"` ✅ |
| 11 | Plugin B parentless create (child) | `"pluginB"` ✅ |

- **Child reuse** (Scenario 8): Plugin B can use its own child as parent — allowed
- **Cross-plugin child denial** (Scenario 9): Plugin A cannot use Plugin B's child — `INVALID_REQUEST`

## Root Cause (if applicable)

`sessions.create` handler in `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions.ts` passes `parentSessionKey` to `createGatewaySession` in `src/gateway/session-create-service.ts`, which resolves the parent session entry but never checks `entry.pluginOwnerId` against the caller's `pluginRuntimeOwnerId`. The matching ownership check (`rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch`) exists for `sessions.delete` but was never mirrored in the create path.

Additionally, even after the initial ownership check was added, the parent-owner recheck inside the lifecycle lock (`createChildSession`) was gated behind `(fork === true || emitCommandHooks === true)`. This left the non-fork parent-link and reset-main paths without lock-time reauthorization, creating a TOCTOU window where a concurrent session delete+recreate could change the parent's owner after the pre-lock check.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

Comprehensive test `"sessions.create rejects cross-plugin or ownerless parent session"` covers all ownership scenarios across fork and non-fork paths. TOCTOU race protection verified by structural code review: the reload+recheck now runs for ALL parent-consuming paths with no yield point between reload and write lock acquisition. Existing fork tests continue to pass.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

None for end users. Plugin runtime authors who inadvertently use cross-plugin or ownerless parent sessions will now receive an `INVALID_REQUEST` error instead of silently receiving cloned transcript data or inheriting session metadata.

## Security Impact (required)

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No — existing `operator.write` scope is sufficient for self-owned sessions
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No — only narrowed: cross-plugin and ownerless parent use is now rejected

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: Linux 4.19.112
- Runtime: Node 22
- Branch: fix/session-fork-ownership-103089 (rebased on latest origin/main)

### Steps

1. Seed a session store entry owned by "pluginA" with a transcript
2. As a caller with `pluginRuntimeOwnerId: "pluginB"` and `operator.write` scope, call `sessions.create({ fork: true, parentSessionKey: "<pluginA's key>" })`
3. Observe the call is rejected with `INVALID_REQUEST`

### Expected

`sessions.create` rejects any cross-plugin or ownerless parent session use with: `Plugin "pluginB" cannot use session "..." as parent because it did not create it.`

### Actual (before fix)

The fork call succeeds and pluginB receives a full copy of pluginA's transcript. Non-fork parent linking also succeeds, leaking metadata and linking the session DAG across owners.

## Evidence

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after
- [x] Trace/log snippets
- [x] Live gateway RPC proof — 10-scenario response table and child ownership persistence in Evidence section above
- [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant)

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: Plugin B forking Plugin A's session (rejected), Plugin B forking ownerless session (rejected), non-plugin client forking any session (allowed), Plugin B non-fork parent linking to Plugin A's session (rejected), Plugin B non-fork parent linking to ownerless session (rejected), Plugin B non-fork parent linking to own session (allowed), Plugin B child has `pluginOwnerId` persisted, Plugin B can reuse its child, Plugin A cannot use Plugin B's child, Plugin B fork child has `pluginOwnerId`, Plugin B parentless create has `pluginOwnerId`
- Edge cases checked: no `pluginRuntimeOwnerId` (skip check), ownerless parent (reject for plugins), self-ownership (allow), `fork === false` with `parentSessionKey` (now gated), child `pluginOwnerId` persistence (fork, non-fork, and parentless), TOCTOU race protection (reload+recheck for all paths)
- What you did NOT verify: Cross-store fork with `targetStorePath`

## Review Conversations

- [x] I addressed ClawSweeper review findings (ownerless protection + non-fork authorization).
- [x] I addressed ClawSweeper P1 TOCTOU race finding: moved reload+owner recheck outside `(fork || emitCommandHooks)` gate, added dedicated recheck in reset-main path.
- [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [x] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — only adds new restrictions for cross-plugin and ownerless parent use; existing self-owned and non-plugin flows unchanged. This matches existing `sessions.delete` behavior.
- [ ] Config/env changes? No
- [ ] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes — the ownership check is placed in `createGatewaySession` at the service layer, close to where the parent session entry is resolved, rather than in the handler. This prevents future callers from accidentally bypassing the check. The unified check (fork + non-fork) mirrors `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` in delete — same rule, same surface. The TOCTOU fix moves the recheck outside the fork/hooks gate, serializing authorization for all parent-consuming paths.
- **Refactor needed**: No — the check is a self-contained change; `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` remains delete-specific (bound to `respond` callback) and is not refactored.
- **Alternative considered**: Adding the check in the `sessions.create` handler (sessions.ts) was simpler but would leave the gap open if `createGatewaySession` is called from other paths. Keeping the fork-only check would leave non-fork parent linking and ownerless sessions unprotected.

## AI Assistance 🤖

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Co-Authored-By**: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes

target.title: feat(ui-i18n): localize Settings toolbar chrome strings (#46217 partial)
target.body:
## Summary

Phase 1 of #46217: replaces 20 hardcoded English strings in the Settings view toolbar with `t()` calls under a new `settings.*` namespace in `ui/src/i18n/locales/en.ts`. Runs `pnpm ui:i18n:sync` to regenerate all 18 locale bundles. `zh-CN` and `zh-TW` ship with native-speaker translations (seeded into the TM so they survive future sync runs); other locales fall through to English fallback per the existing no-provider behavior.

Strings covered (toolbar chrome only):
- Mode toggle: `Form`, `Raw`, plus the two toggle tooltips and `Raw mode unavailable for this snapshot`
- Changes badge: `Unsaved changes` (raw mode), `{count} unsaved change` / `{count} unsaved changes` (form mode, sing/plural — fix applied after @clawsweeper review), `No changes`
- Action buttons: `Open`, `Open config file`, `Open {path}` tooltip, `Clear`, `Apply` / `Applying…`, `Update` / `Updating…`
- Search: placeholder, aria-label, clear-search aria-label
- Accordion: `Quick Settings` header
- `Raw mode disabled (snapshot cannot safely round-trip raw text).` notice

The `Save` / `Saving…` button reuses existing `common.save` / `common.saving` keys (which already carry native translations across all locales — `保存` / `保存中…` in zh-CN, `儲存` / `儲存中…` in zh-TW). The sing/plural pair `unsavedChangeCount` / `unsavedChangesCount` follows the repo's existing pattern (`common.checkpoint` / `common.checkpoints`).

## Out of scope (separate PRs to follow)

Per the @clawsweeper review on #46217, the full localization touches three additional surfaces that intentionally are NOT in this PR:

- `SECTION_CATEGORIES` and `SECTION_META` (category and section labels like "Core", "AI & Agents") — defer pending maintainer guidance on whether top-level category names should be localized.
- `src/config/schema.labels.ts` `FIELD_LABELS` — needs a locale-aware API contract change, which the review explicitly says "needs maintainer product/API direction before automation".
- Appearance section chrome (push notifications, theme import, roundness, text size) — separate cohesive sub-area.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: Control UI Settings view toolbar renders English literals regardless of selected locale; this PR routes the toolbar strings (including the form-mode counted-badge sing/plural branch) through `t()` so they respect the active locale, with zh-CN and zh-TW carrying native-speaker translations.

Real environment tested: Local macOS arm64 checkout, node v22.22.3, pnpm 11.1.0, branch `feat/i18n-settings-chrome-46217` at head 37ffcb1beb on top of upstream/main. Vite dev server started with `pnpm ui:dev` (port 5173) and a real Chrome browser session loaded the regenerated `zh-CN` and `zh-TW` locale bundles via the running dev server, including the new form-mode count keys added after the @clawsweeper review.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```
pnpm ui:i18n:sync
pnpm ui:i18n:check
pnpm ui:dev
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/i18n/test/translate.test.ts ui/src/ui/views/config.browser.test.ts ui/src/ui/config-form.browser.test.ts ui/src/ui/views/config-form.search.node.test.ts src/config/schema.test.ts
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs ui/src/i18n/locales/en.ts ui/src/ui/views/config.ts
pnpm tsgo:core
```

After the dev server was up at http://localhost:5173/, a real Chrome browser session loaded the regenerated bundles, dynamically imported `/src/i18n/locales/{en,zh-CN,zh-TW}.ts`, and rendered a live side-by-side preview of the full toolbar with each locale's actual strings — including the new form-mode counted badge variants at count=1, 3, 12, and Save/Saving reading from `common.save` / `common.saving`.

Evidence after fix:

Latest-head (commit 37ffcb1beb) live preview rendered in a real Chrome browser session against the running Vite dev server. Shows the changes badge in all variants required by the new code path (raw / count=1 / count=3 / count=12 / no changes), plus all action buttons including Save/Saving reading from `common.save` / `common.saving`. All three locales side-by-side using the regenerated bundles:

![Settings toolbar i18n preview — count variants + full toolbar — en / zh-CN / zh-TW](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ObliviateRickLin/openclaw/pr-assets-46217/screenshots/settings-i18n-preview-v3.png)

The screenshot shows:
- English baseline (top): `Unsaved changes` / `1 unsaved change` / `3 unsaved changes` / `12 unsaved changes` / `No changes`, plus `Form` / `Raw` / `Open` / `Clear` / `Save` / `Saving…` / `Apply` / `Applying…` / `Update` / `Updating…`, with `Search settings…` placeholder, `Quick Settings` accordion, and `Raw mode disabled…` notice.
- Simplified Chinese (middle): `未保存的更改` / `1 项未保存的更改` / `3 项未保存的更改` / `12 项未保存的更改` / `无更改`, plus `表单` / `原始` / `打开` / `清除` / `保存` / `保存中…` / `应用` / `应用中…` / `更新` / `正在更新…`, with `搜索设置…` placeholder, `快捷设置` accordion, and `原始模式已禁用…` notice.
- Traditional Chinese (bottom): `未儲存的變更` / `1 項未儲存的變更` / `3 項未儲存的變更` / `12 項未儲存的變更` / `無變更`, plus `表單` / `原始` / `開啟` / `清除` / `儲存` / `儲存中…` / `套用` / `套用中…` / `更新` / `正在更新…`, with `搜尋設定…` placeholder, `快速設定` accordion, and `原始模式已停用…` notice.

All badges and buttons fit comfortably; counts substitute correctly into the `{count}` placeholder; sing/plural correctly diverges in English (`change` vs `changes`) while staying identical in Chinese (Chinese doesn't pluralize); ellipses on `Applying…` / `Updating…` and Chinese equivalents render cleanly.

Live runtime read of the regenerated bundles, captured by dynamically importing the modules in the browser dev console against the running Vite dev server:

```
en.settings.unsavedChangeCount       -> "{count} unsaved change"
en.settings.unsavedChangesCount      -> "{count} unsaved changes"
zh_CN.settings.unsavedChangeCount    -> "{count} 项未保存的更改"
zh_CN.settings.unsavedChangesCount   -> "{count} 项未保存的更改"
zh_TW.settings.unsavedChangeCount    -> "{count} 項未儲存的變更"
zh_TW.settings.unsavedChangesCount   -> "{count} 項未儲存的變更"

en.common.save        -> "Save"
en.common.saving      -> "Saving…"
zh_CN.common.save     -> "保存"
zh_CN.common.saving   -> "保存中…"
zh_TW.common.save     -> "儲存"
zh_TW.common.saving   -> "儲存中…"
```

Real `pnpm ui:i18n:check` console output (post-patch, locally on the branch):

```
control-ui-i18n: raw-copy: baseline entries=646
zh-CN: clean (fallbacks=0)
zh-TW: clean (fallbacks=0)
pt-BR: clean (fallbacks=20)
de:    clean (fallbacks=20)
... 16 more locales reporting clean
```

`fallbacks=0` for zh-CN and zh-TW confirms the new keys (including `unsavedChangeCount` and `unsavedChangesCount`) are TM-backed translations, not English fallback. Supplemental signals: vitest 80/80 passed on the @clawsweeper acceptance set, oxlint reported 0 errors on touched files, tsgo:core exited 0.

Observed result after fix: `ui/src/ui/views/config.ts` has no remaining hardcoded chrome strings in the toolbar region, including the previously English-only form-mode count badge. `pnpm ui:i18n:check` no longer reports raw-copy baseline drift for the strings previously listed. `zh-CN` and `zh-TW` locale bundles render the Settings toolbar in native Chinese including the count badge variants and the Save/Saving button text, verified live in a real Chrome dev session against the running Vite dev server. TM entries seeded for both Chinese locales (all 22 new settings.* keys) so the translations persist across future maintainer sync runs.

What was not tested: Full end-to-end Settings interaction with a live OpenClaw gateway (visual verification was done in the live dev server; interaction-level behavior is covered by the vitest browser tests). Other 16 non-Chinese locales — translations fall through to English fallback because no translation provider was configured in this run, matching existing pipeline behavior for new keys. The deferred Phase 2 / Phase 3 scopes listed in the Out of scope section above were also not touched.

## User Impact

The `scripts/test-extension.mjs` tests hard-coded the Firecrawl extension as having exactly two tracked test files. target.body: Closes #104117 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes an issue where inline code blocks emitted by models with attributes—such as `foo()`—lost their backtick wrapping when OpenClaw converted outbound HTML to plain text for channels. The current sanitizer only matched a bare `` opener, so attributed tags fell through to the generic HTML stripper and arrived at the channel as raw text. ## Why This Change Was Made Updated the regex in `src/infra/outbound/sanitize-text.ts` to accept optional attributes on the opening `` tag (`/]*)?>(.*?)<\/code>/gi`), matching the existing treatment of `]*>` and `]*>` in the same function. Added a focused unit test covering `class` and multiple attributes. ## User Impact Users on Telegram, iMessage, IRC, Google Chat, WhatsApp, and other channels that rely on `sanitizeForPlainText` will now see inline code rendered with backticks even when the model produces attributed `` tags, improving readability of code snippets in channel messages. ## Evidence ### Reproduced behavior on current `main` The bug is deterministic from the source: `/(.*?)<\/code>/gi` does not match ``, so the tag is stripped by the generic `HTML_TAG_RE` remover. ### After-fix runtime proof (public SDK export) The patched helper is the same `openclaw/plugin-sdk/channel-outbound` export that Telegram, iMessage, and other channel adapters import at runtime: ```bash $ ./node_modules/.bin/tsx -e "import { sanitizeForPlainText } from 'openclaw/plugin-sdk/channel-outbound'; console.log('attributed:', sanitizeForPlainText('foo()')); console.log('plain:', sanitizeForPlainText('bar()'));" attributed: `foo()` plain: `bar()` ``` ### Unit tests ```bash $ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/outbound/sanitize-text.test.ts ✓ |unit-fast| src/infra/outbound/sanitize-text.test.ts (29 tests) 17ms ``` ### CI note Rebased onto `upstream/main` (`dfa31af0d4`) to resolve the `CHANGELOG.md does not contain a release section for 2026.7.2` failure in the QA Smoke CI build. Related: #95750

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a gateway restart loop where the same interrupted main session can be accepted for automatic recovery on every boot. Supervisor backoff does not make the session healthy, so attempts separated by minutes or hours must still consume one durable recovery budget.

Main-session restart recovery now has one canonical persisted fuse: `SessionEntry.mainRestartRecovery`.

- `automaticAttempts` counts accepted or acceptance-uncertain automatic recoveries since the last non-aborted run settlement on the same session.
- The first three recoveries may dispatch. An exhausted row is tombstoned before a fourth dispatch, with no elapsed-time expiry.
- A recovery attempt is reserved under the session-store writer lock before Gateway dispatch. The reservation is rolled back only when the request is known not to have been accepted; post-dispatch transport uncertainty keeps the attempt charged.
- Gateway admission revalidates the exact session and reservation identity before accepting a recovery run.
- Foreground admissions use a lifecycle-generation-scoped token set to fence concurrent recovery scans. Each admission releases only its own token on unaccepted, undispatched, or settled paths, so overlapping foreground requests cannot expose or permanently suppress recovery.
- A run that reaches normal session-store settlement without `aborted` clears `mainRestartRecovery`, including background progress that does not touch interaction/activity metadata. Session replacement and reset also clear it.
- `restartRecoveryRuns` remains lifecycle suppression only; it is not used to derive the durable retry budget.
- Subagent orphan recovery retains its separate policy: two attempts in the existing two-minute rapid re-wedge window.
- Tombstone state is committed before the best-effort operator notice is sent, so a stale or failed notification cannot race the quarantine decision.
- Doctor reports wedged main and subagent sessions and can clear only stale `abortedLastRun` flags that conflict with an existing tombstone; it does not re-enable automatic recovery.
- Session-store cache identity uses nanosecond `ctime`/`mtime` plus size so same-size writes inside one millisecond cannot hide recovery or Doctor updates.

This adds no public config, environment variable, wire protocol, provider route, or plugin API.

## User Impact

A wedged main session can no longer trigger unbounded automatic resume across Gateway restarts. After three accepted or acceptance-uncertain recovery attempts, OpenClaw quarantines the session before another automatic dispatch and asks the operator to inspect it and use `/new` or reset.

Healthy progress restores the full budget. The fuse does not expire merely because time passes.

## Evidence

Current branch:

```text
base: upstream/main@99ddde87262
head: 2408915c9ce
```

Current-head local static proof:

```text
node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --write src/gateway/server-methods/agent.ts src/gateway/server-methods/agent.test.ts
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/agent.ts src/gateway/server-methods/agent.test.ts

```

The final autoreview reported no accepted/actionable findings. Local runtime tests were intentionally not run because this is contributor/fork code and the repository requires secretless fork CI or sanitized AWS Crabbox; the available sanitized AWS environment had no IMDS role.

- Passed the Gateway test shard, build, lint, production types, test types, guards, dependency checks, and the other PR-relevant jobs.
- The run has two inherited failures that reproduce unchanged on the already-merged #104210: stale `docs/docs_map.md` output for `Resident local STT`, and the missing `core/doctor/local-audio-acceleration` contribution in `doctor-health-contributions.test.ts`. They are outside this PR's diff and were not folded into this branch.

Focused regression coverage in the branch includes:

- cumulative attempts across slow restart intervals and tombstone-before-fourth behavior;
- pre-dispatch rollback versus post-dispatch acceptance uncertainty;
- exact reservation identity and stale scan rejection;
- concurrent foreground owner tokens, per-owner release, and settlement cleanup;
- successful/background progress reset and session reset/replacement cleanup;

target.title: fix(codex): preserve UTF-16 pairs in tool output delta truncation
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Codex streaming tool output display renders a corrupted glyph ("�") when a non-BMP character (emoji like 😀) straddles the 8,000-character progress-message truncation boundary. The raw `.slice(0, remainingChars)` on the emitted delta cuts at a UTF-16 code-unit boundary — when `remainingChars` lands on the HIGH surrogate of a surrogate pair, the truncated progress message carries a dangling `\uD83D` that corrupts the rendered output in the chat transcript.

## Why This Change Was Made

`truncateUtf16Safe` is already imported on line 29 and used at two other call sites in the same file (lines 3413, 3435) for the 10,000-char transcript-output path. This single progress-message call site at line 1447 was missed during the original import. The fix reuses the canonical helper — no new abstraction, no new import.

## User Impact

Streaming tool output in the Codex chat UI no longer renders a corrupted replacement character when model-generated tool output contains emoji characters near the 8,000-character progress limit. ASCII-only output is unaffected.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** A non-BMP character (emoji surrogate pair) that straddles the `TOOL_PROGRESS_OUTPUT_MAX_CHARS` (8,000) boundary in the Codex event projector's `handleOutputDelta` progress-message path must not produce a lone surrogate in the emitted transcript text.

**Real environment tested:** Node.js v22.22.0, x64, linux, OpenClaw checkout at `2d0d06d3f1`

### Evidence after fix — standalone runtime proof

A standalone Node.js script (`proof-codex-projector-runtime.mts`) imports the real `CodexAppServerEventProjector` class directly from `extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.ts`, drives it through `handleNotification` with `verboseLevel: "full"`, and prints the actual `onToolResult` callback text. This is NOT a test framework — it is a real process executing the production code path.

```
── [Case 1] remainingChars=1, delta=😀hello ──
onToolResult calls: 3
[call 0] len=32 lone=false
🛠️ `show emoji.txt (workspace)`
---
[call 1] len=8019 lone=false
🛠️ Bash
```txt
aaaa...aaaa
```
---
[call 2] len=37 lone=false
🛠️ Bash
```txt
...(truncated)...
```
---
── [Case 2] remainingChars=2, delta=x😀y ──
onToolResult calls: 3
[call 0] len=33 lone=false
🛠️ `show emoji2.txt (workspace)`
---
[call 1] len=8018 lone=false
🛠️ Bash
```txt
aaaa...aaaa
```
---
[call 2] len=39 lone=false
🛠️ Bash
```txt
x
...(truncated)...
```
---

=== RUNTIME PROOF COMPLETE ===
node=v22.22.0
No lone surrogates in any emitted progress text.
Fix confirmed: truncateUtf16Safe in production projector.
```

**Case 1** — remainingChars=1, delta starts with 😀: `truncateUtf16Safe` detects the HIGH surrogate at position 0 and backs off, producing an empty chunk. The progress message is `...(truncated)...` — clean, no surrogate bytes.

**Case 2** — remainingChars=2, delta="x😀y": `truncateUtf16Safe` cuts at position 1 (the 'x'), backs off before the emoji at positions 1-2. The progress message is `x\n...(truncated)...` — clean, no surrogate bytes.

### Negative control (pre-fix behavior reproduced)

Same standalone script, same environment. `event-projector.ts` reverted to `origin/main` (`.slice(0, remainingChars)`) — the script picks up the old code via tsx on-the-fly compilation:

```
── [Case 1] remainingChars=1, delta=😀hello ──

target.title: fix(feishu): drive info finds files past the first page
target.body:
Closes #93928

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Feishu users running `feishu_drive info` received `File not found` for files that were not present on the first page of the root drive listing.

## Why This Change Was Made

Drive info now queries Feishu's metadata API directly by file token and type instead of searching a single root-list response. Shortcut lookups retain the existing root-list behavior because the metadata endpoint does not support the shortcut type, and installations without the metadata scope fall back to the legacy lookup for compatibility.

## User Impact

Users can retrieve metadata for supported files regardless of the containing shared folder or root-list page. Existing read-only installations continue to support root-level info lookups, while direct lookups require `drive:drive.metadata:readonly` or the full `drive:drive` scope.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test extensions/feishu/src/drive.test.ts` — 24 tests passed
- `pnpm test:extension feishu` — 79 files and 1,123 tests passed
- Focused oxfmt and oxlint checks passed
- Documentation formatting and `git diff --check` passed
- Final Codex review reported no findings

### Redacted live Feishu proof

Validated on July 11, 2026 with an enabled enterprise app using application-identity `drive:drive.metadata:readonly`. No App Secret, tenant token, file token, title, owner ID, or URL is included below.

For an existing wiki document, Feishu resolved the wiki token to its underlying document metadata:

```json
{"httpStatus":200,"code":0,"metasCount":1,"returnedType":"docx","tokenLength":27,"hasTitle":true,"hasUrl":true,"requestType":"wiki","requestTokenMatches":true}
```

The PR's exact direct lookup shape was then used with that underlying `docx` token:

```json
{"httpStatus":200,"code":0,"metasCount":1,"tokenMatched":true,"returnedType":"docx","hasTitle":true,"hasUrl":true,"hasOwner":true,"hasCreateTime":true,"hasModifyTime":true}
```

The same app does not have the legacy root-list scope, so the old root request returned HTTP 400 / Feishu code `99991672`, while the direct metadata request above succeeded. This confirms direct info lookup works independently with the documented metadata-only scope.

An invalid `docx` token returned HTTP 200 with top-level `code: 0`, an empty `metas` array, and this per-document failure:

```json
{"failed_list":[{"code":970005,"token":"<redacted-invalid-token>"}]}
```

The missing-file regression test now mirrors that observed `failed_list` shape and confirms the tool reports `File not found`. Shortcut behavior and the legacy read-only fallback remain covered by focused mocked SDK tests; no existing app with exactly `drive:drive:readonly` and without metadata scope was available for a live fallback test.

After rebasing onto current `main`, production/test type checks are blocked by pre-existing errors in `extensions/feishu/src/presentation-card.ts` (`renderMessagePresentationTableFallbackText` missing and an unrelated `select`/`table` comparison). This PR does not modify that file.

target.title: fix(extensions/anthropic): preserve migrated model entries when inherited keys shadow converted refs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where adopting Claude CLI auth could silently drop a model's custom settings (aliases, parameters, etc.) or throw when the global `Object.prototype` contains an inherited property matching the converted Anthropic model ref.

## Why This Change Was Made

`rewriteModelEntryMap` used `converted in next` to decide whether to copy a legacy `claude-cli/*` entry to its Anthropic equivalent, and then assigned with `next[converted] = value`. The `in` operator follows the prototype chain, and the assignment can throw or invoke an inherited setter when `Object.prototype` is polluted. The migration could therefore skip the copy, delete the original `claude-cli/*` key, and lose the user's model configuration.

The change now:
- checks own-property membership with `Object.hasOwn`;
- writes migrated and seeded entries with `Object.defineProperty` so they become own properties even when `Object.prototype` has a getter-only accessor, non-writable data descriptor, or setter.

This applies the same own-entry invariant that #103373 adds to the Anthropic API-key default-allowlist seeding path.

## User Impact

Users whose runtime has a polluted `Object.prototype` no longer lose per-model aliases or other metadata, and no longer see migration throws, when adopting Claude CLI-backed Anthropic refs.

## Evidence

### Unit tests

```bash
pnpm test extensions/anthropic/cli-migration.test.ts --run
```

Result: 19 passed.

The regression suite covers four Object.prototype descriptor collisions and fails against the parent commit:
- inherited writable data descriptor;
- inherited non-writable data descriptor (throws before the fix);
- inherited getter-only accessor (throws before the fix);
- inherited setter accessor (entry becomes undefined before the fix, setter is not invoked after).

### Type / lint

```bash
pnpm tsgo:extensions        # exit 0
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json extensions/anthropic/cli-migration.test.ts extensions/anthropic/cli-migration.ts
```

Both pass.

### Live migration proof

Controlled run with an `Object.prototype` getter-only accessor shadowing the converted ref:

```text
=== Claude CLI auth adoption migration proof ===
Scenario: Object.prototype has a getter-only accessor for the converted ref.
Migrated entry: {
  "alias": "Work Opus",
  "temperature": 0.7,
  "agentRuntime": { "id": "claude-cli" }
}
Entry is own property: true
Alias preserved: true
Parameters preserved: true
```

The alias and `temperature` parameter survive migration, and the resulting entry is an own property of `models` rather than the inherited accessor value.

## Release Note

- Anthropic: preserve migrated model aliases and parameters when inherited prototype keys shadow converted Claude CLI refs.

Related: #103373

## Summary

This PR tightens the existing compatible-bundle MCP path for bundles that need a narrower default tool surface.

- Adds regression coverage that a Codex-compatible bundle `.mcp.json` preserves `toolFilter.include`, `toolFilter.exclude`, and a relative bundle data root.
- Documents bundle MCP tool filters on the plugin-bundles page alongside the existing transport and tool-naming guidance.
- Keeps scope limited to bundle MCP loading/docs; runtime filtering behavior already exists and is covered separately.

Reviewers should focus on whether the bundle MCP docs accurately describe the existing runtime behavior and whether the new compatible-bundle regression is useful.

## Linked context

Related precedent investigated: bundle MCP support and follow-up coverage in prior OpenClaw PRs such as #48611, #71287, #79686, and #88399. This PR follows that existing bundle MCP seam.

target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

target.title: fix(feishu): use union_id as fallback for @mention detection in multi-bot groups
target.body:
## Problem

Fixes #40768

When multiple Feishu bots share the same group, @mentioning a specific bot is not recognized. The bot logs `message in group ... did not mention bot` even though it's correctly mentioned.

## Root Cause

Feishu `open_id` is **app-scoped** — the same bot has a different `open_id` depending on which app's token is used to query it. Confirmed by querying the same message with two different bot tokens:

```
# Same @mention, different app contexts:
writer token → mention open_id: ou_4ede388c79638a9057a432c3e3832f91
tron token   → mention open_id: ou_04dc13327d491d9e36da57826a4131f0
```

WebSocket push events deliver mention `open_id`s in a specific app context that may not match the receiving bot's own `open_id`, causing `checkBotMentioned()` to always return `false`.

## Fix

`union_id` is globally unique across all apps for the same entity — it doesn't vary by app context. This PR:

1. Fetches `union_id` alongside `open_id` from `bot/v3/info` at startup
2. Stores it in a new `botUnionIds` map in monitor state
3. Passes it through to `checkBotMentioned()` as a fallback
4. Matches mentions by `union_id` when `open_id` doesn't match

The `open_id` match is preserved as the primary check; `union_id` is a fallback, so existing behavior is unchanged for single-bot setups.

## Files Changed

- `types.ts`: add `botUnionId` to `FeishuProbeResult`
- `probe.ts`: extract `union_id` from `bot/v3/info` response
- `monitor.startup.ts`: propagate `botUnionId` through `FeishuMonitorBotIdentity`
- `monitor.state.ts`: add `botUnionIds` map with proper clear/delete
- `monitor.account.ts`: store/clear `botUnionId`, pass to `handleFeishuMessage`
- `bot.ts`: accept `botUnionId` in `checkBotMentioned` and `parseFeishuMessageEvent`, match by `union_id` when `open_id` mismatches
